risks.note: The MD&A states the industry is highly fragmented across organised and unorganised players, that the attractiveness and large potential of the opportunity is driving competition in India up significantly, and explicitly that there are no entry barriers in the industry, exposing the Company to new entrants. With no structural barrier, pricing and win rates in both the SaaS and advisory verticals are permanently contestable.
risks.risk: No entry barriers and a highly fragmented, intensifying competitive field

risks.note: Management names reliance on technology as a weakness alongside its digital-innovation strength: disruption in the digital infrastructure would hit the SaaS products, the marketplace and the monitoring offering, which are the Company's core delivery mechanism.
risks.risk: Dependence on digital platforms and technology infrastructure

risks.note: Listed as a threat in the SWOT: rapid advances in solar technology or shifts in digital platforms could force continuous re-investment to stay current. For an asset-light software business this is a recurring cost and obsolescence risk, and the Directors' Report states expenditure on research and development was 'None' for the year.
risks.risk: Rapid technological shifts requiring continuous adaptation and investment

risks.note: The MD&A names regulatory changes as a possible threat and the SWOT states that changes in solar energy policies, tariffs or regulations could affect demand for solar solutions. A large part of the business — advisory contracts from public-sector bodies and development corporations, and the government-facing SaaS for distributed renewable programmes — sits directly on government programme continuity.
risks.risk: Policy, tariff and regulatory dependence of demand

risks.note: Management flags lower brand recognition due to the Company's relatively recent founding (established 2017) and market-penetration challenges, which in a competitive, tender-driven advisory market affects the ability to win and price work.
risks.risk: Limited brand recognition and market penetration for a young company

risks.note: Management frames timely completion as critical in the renewable industry: delays raise cost overruns and expose the Company to penalties and liquidated damages. The Company's stated moat is its execution record (it says it has never been penalised for delayed execution), so a slip both costs money and removes the differentiator; 'Timely completion of Orders' is the first item in its stated key strategy.
risks.risk: Execution and contracted-schedule risk on projects

risks.note: The MD&A states that all activities revolve around the main business with no separate reportable business segment. The report contradicts itself on geography — the same MD&A says all operations are conducted within India with no separate reportable geographical segment, while its SWOT claims the Company operates in multiple countries including India, UAE and Germany — so the extent of international diversification cannot be determined from this bundle; on either reading, revenue concentration in solar-linked services is undiluted.

The Company says its principal assets are its employees and that manpower has been the driving force of growth, with total employees on roll at 80 as on 31st March 2026. In an advisory and software business of this size, key-person and attrition exposure is structural, and the Company is subject to the risk framework described in the Directors' Report rather than any disclosed attrition metric.
risks.risk: Dependence on a small employee base for a people-led business
